library.name: Wire
library.author: Arduino
library.sentence: This library allows you to communicate with I2C and Two Wire Interface devices.
library.paragraph: It allows the communication with I2C devices like temperature sensors, realtime clocks and many others using SDA (Data Line) and SCL (Clock Line).

library.name: Servo
library.author: Michael Margolis, Arduino
library.sentence: Allows Arduino boards to control a variety of servo motors.
library.paragraph:
This library can control a great number of servos.
It makes careful use of timers: the library can control 12 servos using only 1 timer.
On the Arduino Due you can control up to 60 servos.

library.name: EEPROM
library.author: Arduino, Christopher Andrews
library.sentence: Enables reading and writing to the permanent board storage.
library.paragraph: This library allows to read and write data in a memory type, the EEPROM, that keeps its content also when the board is powered off. The amount of EEPROM available depends on the microcontroller type.

library.name: HID
library.author: Arduino
library.sentence: Module for PluggableUSB infrastructure. Exposes an API for devices like Keyboards, Mice and Gamepads.

library.name: SPI
library.author: Arduino
library.sentence: Enables the communication with devices that use the Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) Bus.
library.paragraph: SPI is a synchronous serial data protocol used by microcontrollers for communicating with one or more peripheral devices quickly over short distances. It uses three lines common to all devices (MISO, MOSI and SCK) and one specific for each device.

library.name: SoftwareSerial
library.author: Arduino
library.sentence: Enables serial communication on any digital pin.
library.paragraph: The SoftwareSerial library has been developed to allow serial communication on any digital pin of the board, using software to replicate the functionality of the hardware UART. It is possible to have multiple software serial ports with speeds up to 115200 bps.
